methodology.methodDefinition: Quantify how many compatible client devices still need CyberSmart, by school and device type, while also showing current pass/fail evidence.
methodology.evidenceImpact: Separate analysis only; no application or database changes.
methodology.recommendedUse: Use Site Gap Summary and Device Type Gaps for rollout planning.

methodology.methodDefinition: Read-only export of 10,273 client-compute records representing 10,385 devices.
methodology.recommendedUse: Treat inventory as the coverage denominator, subject to normal asset reconciliation.

methodology.methodDefinition: 34 CSV exports supplied by the user; 33 unique file hashes analysed. The portal screenshot shows 5,518 total devices, 2,129 secure and 5,094 recently active.
methodology.recommendedUse: Do not add raw row counts: each device has multiple check rows.

methodology.methodDefinition: The portal total is split as 5,270 installed/reporting devices represented by detailed exports plus 248 Pending devices.
methodology.recommendedUse: Treat 248 as the CyberSmart Pending status. Do not confuse it with the separate inventory installation gap.

methodology.methodDefinition: Grouped primarily by CyberSmart Device ID, with serial/hostname fallback only when Device ID is absent.
methodology.evidenceImpact: 5,270 unique CyberSmart devices found across unique exports.
methodology.recommendedUse: Use unique device counts, not check-result rows.

methodology.methodDefinition: For duplicate/current exports, the latest Last Check In row is selected for each device/check. Fail if any latest check is Fail. Pass only when all latest checks are Pass. Non-Pass/Fail values are retained as Unknown / incomplete.
methodology.evidenceImpact: 2,074 passing and 3,196 failing devices in the supplied exports. The supplied Result column contains Pass and Fail only.
methodology.recommendedUse: Remediate Failed Checks; reconcile the CSV-derived pass count to the portal Secure headline.

methodology.methodDefinition: Windows clients, Chromebooks/ChromeOS, Apple/Mac, iPads/iOS and Android/tablets. Screens, signage and phones are excluded. Windows Server is shown in CyberSmart results but excluded from the client-device installation gap.
methodology.recommendedUse: Use server evidence separately from client rollout.

methodology.methodDefinition: Inventory installation gap = max(compatible inventory quantity - unique compatible CyberSmart devices reported for that site/type, 0). This is a calculated deployment-coverage measure and is not the CyberSmart Pending status.
methodology.recommendedUse: Use Installation Gap as the rollout work queue; investigate overages and shared/central allocations.

methodology.methodDefinition: Normalized exact serial match first; exact asset-tag to CyberSmart hostname second. Ambiguous duplicate matches are not treated as exact. Client-match totals exclude server/other CyberSmart records and require the report site to agree with the matched inventory school.
methodology.evidenceImpact: 2,566 compatible client devices matched exactly within the same school.
methodology.recommendedUse: Use Exact Matches for strong one-to-one evidence; filter School agrees? = Yes and exclude Server for the client-only subset.

methodology.methodDefinition: Inventory categories containing 'unmanaged' are flagged as possible installations when the category is compatible-looking. Unmanaged screens, signage and phones remain excluded.
methodology.recommendedUse: Confirm ownership, supportability and device type before deployment.

methodology.methodDefinition: Installed counts are never subtracted below zero. Any CyberSmart count above inventory is shown as Installed over inventory.
methodology.recommendedUse: Reconcile source inventory, site assignment and central/shared devices.

methodology.methodDefinition: The workbook reflects the supplied exports and current read-only inventory snapshot at generation time.
methodology.recommendedUse: Refresh both sources before using as certification evidence.
